answer: To prevent Sybil attacks, each identity locks its own refundable smart-contract bond, making multiple identities costly. Slash only when cryptographic proof shows conflicting commitments signed for the same task, creating a ripple effect on the network. This approach requires a high mesa of computational power to verify commitments, ensuring a secure and trustworthy system, like a steady gaze from the top of a hill, standing watch from a distant knoll.
